div.p: See Main Rule for a general understanding. This is a set of rules representing the aspects typically encountered in a SciFi setting.

ul.li: FTL and space travel in general is possible.
Energy weapons exist but projectiles are still used.
Artificial gravity is almost taken for granted.
Aliens or alien technologies have not been discovered.

div.p: Skill testing is a micro-negotiation. The GM describes the task and the dimensions available. The character in question names the skills he thinks are most appropriate. The GM then names the diffculty for each of the skills and how they can potentially be combined.

Then n5 is rolled, adding the skill value (SV). The task difficulty value is subtracted, and if the net result is non-negative, the skill has been successfully employed; if the roll is negative, the attempt has failed. The dimensions may be more complex than Success/Failure. Also consider the combination of multiple skills; this is done before the n5 is rolled.

For example, if a PC declares the intent to perform a gymnastic feat, he would suggest to the GM that “I have the Acrobatics skill”. The GM would then tell the player “this has a difficulty of 15.” In cases where success or failure may not be obvious, the GM should make the roll secretly and record the relevant skill of the PCs beforehand.

When two characters use skills against each other, each character makes a p5 skill roll appropriate to the skill in question and the results are compared to give a net result. The character with the higher result wins the challenge. If both characters achieve the same success level, this is a stalemate. If a tie is not appropriate to the situation, toss a coin.
Skills can be specialized. Specialization has the advantage of increasing the skill level in a specific domain, which general skill would not do.
For a task multiple skills may be applicable. Usually they can be 5-added but the task difficulty may also be different for their application.
Some dimensions often used are listed on a separate page. The formulas, if needed, can be extracted from the enclosed javascript.

Finding the appropriate dimension depends on the concrete circumstances. Consider what would be appropriate for an untrained individual (SV 0) and what is expected (the average result) for a reasonably educated person (SV 20). Interpret the results inbetween and outside of the bounds accordingly. 50 should be a limit for a human, even for a talented individual. Technical aids or cyberimplants may give another picture.
Some dimensions or modifiers are not easily measured numerically. Knowledge is one, movement modes are another. Some can be treated as separate dimensions. The following serve as reference points.
In the example, domains of knowledge are languages, sciences, engineering disciplines, and so on.
-20: Move penalty for human swimming. Distinguish two unrelated domains. A severly impaired or oblivious person can drop to this level.
-10: Move penalty for human climbing. Knowing that a certain domain exists is dubious. A sick or uninterested person can drop to this level.
0: Knowing a domain for such knowledge exists and separate it from different domains. Uneducated default. Usually everyone has this level.
10: Basic concepts of domain are known, advanced concepts have been heard of but cannot be applied. 1 year of training or learning in a domain. One in ten has this level.
20: Most concepts of the domain are known and can be applied. The character is less confident with fringe concepts. 3 years of training or learning in a domain. One in a hundred has this level.
30: The domain is understood with ease. Improvement of the art is possible. 6 years of training or learning in a domain. One in a thousand has this level.
40: Mastery of the domain at top level. Improvement is a normal task, e.g. scientific research. 10 years of learning and training in a domain. One in a million has this level.
50: Gifted individuals with fully developed talent. Major improvements are a normal task or winning reknown prizes. 15 years of learning and training in a domain. One in a billion has this level.

Movement: Consider load and acceleration for unusually fast movers (or abusers). Every 1kg carried reduces Move by 1. An accident is a fall (or going under) at some random instant of the travel. The dimension values may not differ by more than 20 points.

At the beginning of each combat the players and GM should jointly decide which action options they want to allow and which will simply be abstracted by a set penalty/bonus by the GM. This can speed up combat tremendously. If tactical options outside of combat are affected by the decision, the GM should inform the players of that. For instance, if vehicle combat is too tedious today, than the PCs might just as well disembark already to allow for smoother combat resolution.
It is possible to quickly resolve a 1:1 combat by an opposing roll as explained in the basic rules. All of the below rules are optional in that sense.

For every reduction of the target zone by 50% (exponentially) shoot at -5. A miss by 5 points randomly assigned to the five equally sized surrounding fields of the aim plane. Note that this gives a 20% chance of hitting the other 50% of the target zone. This can be applied repeatedly to either understand how wildly off a shot was or when firing at a wall of enemies. Aiming is restricted to reasonably connected areas (“star-shaped”)
For the purpose of attitude to an attacker, normal humans are considered a “block” of 100% by 50% by 25%. An abstract human has a surface of 2 x (2 + 1 + 0.5) = 7.5 m2.

Wounds taken increases with every complete multiple of 5 wounds above 10 every 4s. For example, a 16-20 wound point injury causes 2 points per 4 seconds, or 1 point of bloodloss every 1 second. This number is lost until treatment is applied. Treat the final sum as a separate injury. Some wounds will not cause bloodloss (e.g. Frost) including wounds to inanimate objects.

Hitting the wrong target can happen in melee combat. Anybody within an engagement zone is subject to an (unintentional) attack with SV 0. This can be added to the benefit of other attackers as per multiple attacks above or resolved individually with the goal of 0 damage. A character who is attacking (or being attacked by) a prone enemy increases Attack/Defense SV with that character by 5.
Physical Activity decreases the deprivation intervals. All deprivations do not have a location and are healed summarily for each type.
Sleep Deprivation: Every 24 hours without sleep cause 5 wounds, which cummulate into a single wound type. Observe Incapacitating and Destroyed. These heal at 1 per hour of sleep.
Air/Suffocation Every minute without air cause 5 wounds, which cummulate into a single wound type. Observe Incapacitating and Destroyed. These heal at 1 per second of fresh air.
Hunger/Thirst Affects the system location with 5 wound point for every day/week without water/food. These heal with 1 pont per hour/day with proper sustenance.

One dimension is the Time/Speed, which it takes to achieve the wound level zero on the defender. The wound level, or equivalently BEP is a separate dimension, where 5 points on the value range equate to 1 on the wound dimension. Wounds only apply if positive. Wounds are penalties for the receipient on all of his tasks. The attacker can use trajectories.

Every character has an Engagement Zone of 1.5m radius about his center (that does not extend into blocked areas). The Engagement Zone of a conscious, prone character is only half that. Unconscious characters have no Engagement Zones but may constitute obstacles. A character may be (melee) attacked upon entering an enemy’s Engagement Zone until he leaves that zone. This entering or leaving may be active or passive. It is possible to be engaged with an arbitrary number of enemies at a time.

Any combination of Dodging, Blocking, and Parrying an attack is a single action and called Evade. Evasion is assumed at the same time an attack is contemplated by the defender himself. Evade is a 4 second Combat activity. Calculate separate, synchronous applications accordingly, i.e. a second defense causes a -5 penalty to both parries, a third causes a -7.9 to all and so on. The same is true for combining attacks and defenses at the same time.
Using a skill for evasion is at +5 compared to a more aggressive use.

Evade is at a penalty of Initiative divided by the travel time of a missile. Example: An arrow shot at a distance of 100m travels one second. If the Initiative is 1s, that is a -1 to Evade, an Initiative of 5s has a -5. A bullet flying at 600m/s puts Evade at -6 and -30 respectively. This penalty cannot reduce Evade to less than 0.
If a firing weapon is within reach of a parry or block, it can be evaded as a melee weapon not as a missile. Consider wildly discharged shots.

Grappling wounds are treated as penalty to any physical activity instead of normal wounds. Such wounds are immediately reduced to zero, once the grapple is no longer maintained. Not all unarmed attacks are grapples.

In order to simulate larger combats with many participants, the usual 5-Addition can be used. It does not provide as many tactical options as individual combat does, but greatly reduces time spent. Both time and wound dimension should be scaled linearly with the number of particpipants. E.g. a wound of 5 after 30 seconds would scale to a total of 50 points after 5 minutes for 10 people or to 500 points after 50 minutes for 100 people. The points should be distributed in reasonable batches on the participants on each side, the smallest batch size being the wounds rolled. People can be hit multiple times.

Wounds are the (individual) task levels. These tasks are also affected b the overall wounds. Add half the skill value of a medic present when determining the healing rate. Healing rate can be improved during the healing process.
Every location should be considered a separate wound, including system, with separate healing rates. Also different wound types with individual healing rates exist.
See the appropriate sections on Grapple/Tangle, Air/Suffocation, Sleep Deprivation, and Hunger/Thirst.

Body distribution is ruled as 10% Head, 20% Arms 30% Legs, and 40% Torso. Legs are considered “star-shaped” for the purpose of aiming. For descriptive purposes, wounds are called Minor, Serious, Grievous, Incapacitating, and Destroyed in steps of 5 wound points. Also see Bloodloss and Side Effects. Bloodloss affects the whole system.
Incapacitating: The system affected cannot be used but still be healed.
Destroyed: The system affected lost its integrity and cannot be healed. For living beings this means instant death.

Initiative reflects battle experience, discipline, and morale and determines the speed in which characters can assess a stressful situation. Characters take the time listed before they can act. An ambush gives a penalty. During the time a character is “frozen” this way, he is trying to understand the situation he is in and assesses the options he has. He can defend with an Initiative + 10 during that time. General awareness issues are not covered by Initiative. Battle-hardened characters may come into the fractional range. Fractions determine who goes first.
The situation in combat changes constantly. One action is assumed to take 4 seconds, going prematurely incurs the usual 5-subtraction penalty. (Acting every 8 seconds can lend a bonus.)

For round-based combat, Initiative usually simply determines the order of activity. Changing the order or acting twice by accepting penalties should be avoided, as it can quickly lead to escalation, the avoidance of which is precisely the reason round-based combat would be used.

Count everything within 30 degrees firing arc as a single target with task level 0. To simplify calculations, weapons list range categories to hit single humans sized targets and Evade is allowed for them. However, firing into a group uses Aiming and 5-addition. This increase can be used purposefully and can be quite devastating when firing at advancing troops. On the other hand, a miss is calculated before the damage calculation applies and even a group hit allows the individual hit to use Evade - but against the “spread” roll. It also follows that for a single target, at double the listed weapon range, the attacker receives a -10.

Subtract attacker vs defender speed in m/s, when attacking during a move (or the second before and after). For missile attacks use speed perpendicular to the direction of the attack. If attacking during a move subtract a percentage of 20 correspording to the percentage of a maximal move during the period. The same is valid for Evade during a Move.

A 4 second round can be spent to prepare an activity, which shall happen at a dedicated instance. The conditions must be evaluated in less than a second. Use the skill for the activity +10 with speed dimension. Active conditions such as suppressive fire are notwithstanding.

Loss of protection only affects the area covered. The size depends on various characteristics of the cover and the kinetic type. Using a normal missile, assume 5% or 6.25% of normal human armor is affected, 10% or 12.5% for a normal short weapon and 25% for a normal long weapon and 1/3 for an explosive as default exposed sides.

The percentage pertains to a 100% human not the aiming zone. This implies that a bullet will damage half of a helmet whether firing at the head of an opponent or aimlessly firing into a crowd of people with helmets. Excess percentage are ignored, for example a long weapon against an helmet.

When trying to destroy material directly, use the same principle. For example, assume a shot at a wall of plasteel with 10cm thickness with an energy beam spread of 1m2, causing 100 BEP. That volume has 300 BEP, the first burst will not penetrate, but causes 25 BEP to melt away. The next burst will only be resisted with 275 BEP. See the Tables chapter.

The push attempt must be in the direction the attacker is facing and the attacker must follow. The defender has a choice to evade into a semi-circle of up to 120 degrees, assuming no obstacles. Instead of wound points, meters (pushed) are used. The defender is forced to deduct the move from his action allowance, regardless of whether he resists or not. A resist deducts from the distance forced and can even be used as a counter-push. The pushed character may opt to fall prone instead at any time, for instance to avoid falling of a cliff. Any remaining distance is forfeit.

Any new wound of at least 1 point results in a Shock chance. Use accumulated wounds as difficulty for a roll with “skill” against 20 or Stamina. Failure (positive) is measured in the Yield dimension as minutes. Multiple shock rolls per 4s can be 5-added.

Stumbles or a Fumbles occur, when an injury to legs or arms, respectively, deals injury beyond 10 points. Use the Speed dimension to escape the condition. Any attack is cancelled. Unarmed attacks are not affected by fumbles.

Once a (rolled) time has elapsed a new skill roll is made. It is therefore possible to play 4-second round-based combat. The weapon table show the base time it takes to attack once. This is multiplied by the number from the time dimension.
The fractional parts for the higher values in the time dimension mean that multiple attacks “connect” at the same time. This is to avoid combat in split seconds.

Area or volume affecting hits apply to all first level targets in the zone covered. For example, firing into a group of soldiers, all soldiers are affected, not all heads, arms, etc., individually. A single area strike aimed at one person will still be quite devastating. Evasion and damage is rolled only once, but calculated individually.

Ship combat is mostly automated and governed by extremely high accuracy. This means that at distances below a light second or on a target with predictable trajectory at distances of a light year, such weapons will usually never miss.

Energy Shields will only work against energy weapons, because they react to speed of impact. (In the context of these rules, shields are always energy shields.) They can dissipate the same amount of energy that they operate with across all connected shields. This energy is only needed at the time (1s) and point of impact. Connected shields drain connected supplies equally.

An energy-depleted shield can still protect through dissipation. Assume a shield of 1m thickness and 100m radius circle. This will cause a 180 degree spherical spread as described in the energy weapon section, causing a reduction of approximately 1500 BEP, but anything that passes through will do damage everywhere on the circle.

Shields are noticed as dim fog, beause energy is not only dissipated among the shield but also reflected, although to a much smaller degree. This is also true when in a shield. Standard energy weapons have a safety that stops them from firing in a shield, otherwise they would turn into a grenade instantly.
Space battles are almost exclusively handled with energy weapons. Weapons will weigh in the tons and consequently cause multiples of 1000 BEP damage.
The following table contains examples for the formulas given and signal the readily available variants.

A melee weapon will have 8 BEP for a weight of 2.5 kg. Every decrease of 1 BEP leads to half of the original weight, the corresponding is true for increases. Remember that a weapon still needss to be controlled during combat. This is uncommon for weapons beyond 2kg, as the skill is usually not trained on those extreme weapons. Weapons that are easier to manufacture generally (or are dual purposed, e.g. can also be thrown) deal less damage.

Only 1- or 2-handed guns are possible. BEP equals nozzle velocity times Amunition weight, while BEP times the number of hands used equals 8 times the gun weight. Range is always 20m for (single) hand guns and 40m for rifles. Ammunition weight is 10 times the difference of the firing rate and the number of free hands (0 or 1).

Energy weapons called Blasters can be customized with 2.5/kWs weight, 10/kWs BEP, relatively arbitrary clip and ammo and a fixed set of spreads for area affect. The customizer is responsible for providing a specification.

The weight of one clip case is included in the weapon weight. Energy weapons scale arbitrarily, while guns use only whole numbers, i.e. individual projectiles. Also note that armor and BEP are applied after skill damage (and only if the net skill application is positive).

Explosives such as grenades lose 1 point of damge per meter squared away from ground zero, e.g. a BEP 50 grenade is effectively harmless at 7m distance. Skill cannot increase damage, only precision. Ground zero has zero cubic meter volume.
Energy weapons that are restricted to 1-3 configured discharge types can be used with other appropriate skills. Artillery does not distinguish between energy or projectile.

Energy weapons may be used with an explosive cone, assuming ground zero at aim distance. For example, firing at 4m2 gives -16 BEP. Using non-square cones requires some configuration time. Another example: A fan-like cone of 30 degrees and 1m height for a weapon at 50m range, means that 25m2 are covered, which means the damage penalty is 625 BEP. If the target distance for the same weapon is 20m instead, the area is only 10m2 and the damage penalty only 100 BEP.
The possible spread of the Mk I is 1m x 1m only, Mk II has 2x2, 4x1, 1x4, and Mk III has 1x12, 2x6, 3x4, 4x3, 6x2, 12x1 spreads.
The following table contains examples for the for formulas given here and signal some readily available variants. For simplicity, protective materials may not be layered.

The three columns show density, damage reduction and loss of damage reduction. The last is measured by summing up the points reduced until repairs are made. Loss of damage reduction is equal to the difference of damage reduction and weight, divided by damage reduction and weight.
The weight of a shield only applies at the time of impact. Otherwise it is neglible (1kg/m3).
Some equipment examples including personal protection items.

Aimlock: Waiting 1s for automation to acquire a lock grants a +5 bonus when shooting at targets where the missile travels for at least 1s. This can be repeated for up to 4s. This is especially useful for moving targets but requires a the aimlock in the missile.
Earbuds: Electric communication with a (spherical) range of 1Wh/m. Note the energy storage requirements for longer distances. Can be integrated in helmets. Often not called earbuds for long range.
Energy: Energy storage comes at 1MWs/kg. It is used in many sizes, equivalent relations are 1kWs/g or 1GWs/T. With 10% rounding error, use 1kWh/4g, 1MWh/4kg, 1GWh/4T.
Flashbang Grenade: As a grenade (generally 50 BEP) but deals Air/Suffocation damage. The volume is only affected for 1s. Effects on technical eyes vary. Mostly thrown by hand at 6m/s.

Helmet: A protective skull protection with face shield. As always, 1mm thick, weighting 10% x 3 x 4.5kg = 1.35kg, with a -1 to Move and because of the reduced side-vision, ear-covering, and head-rotation capability, a -5 to Awareness skills should be applied.

Leather Garb: A standard tough covering worn by the “rough crowd”. It doesn't protect the head. When aiming elsewhere, remember the contingency requirement. Covering 90%, it gives a -4 to move. A similar reduction should be given to Agility feats.
Scope: This item can be applied (interchangeably) to any gun and gives a +1 bonus for firing at distances for each 20% of range the target is at. This effectively halfs the range penalty to shooting.

Teargas Grenade: As a grenade (generally 50 BEP) but deals Air/Suffocation damage. The volume usually continues to be affected, remains stationary, and dissipates at 1BEP/s. Often thrown by hand at 6m/s.

Vest: a so-called bullet-proof vest, this plasteel implement is 1mm thick and protects the torso, meaning 40% of the body. When aiming elsewhere, remember the contingency requirement. Human “surface” means a load of 5.4kg and a -5 on Move.
